functions.get_item(sku: str): returns dict {"sku": str, "name": str, "price": float (dollars, e.g. 12.5 = $12.50), "category": str} or None if sku unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id: str): returns dict {"id": str, "name": str, "discount": float (fraction, e.g. 0.10 = 10% off list price), "region": str} or None if id unknown

value.notes: pricing.py only supplies rates/prices; it does not apply discounts or round amounts. Sales tax is not handled here (tax.py, agent2). Customer region is supplied so tax.py can look it up from customer data passed by invoice.py.

why: Defines the pricing API for the team, using team standard (dollars as float, percentages as fractions, missing lookup returns None).

value.lines: list of (category: str, amount_cents: int) tuples, one per order line; amount_cents is the line amount before tax and discount
value.region: customer region code string as in data_tax/rates.csv (e.g. "TX"), or None for an unknown customer
value.discount_pct: customer discount as a percent number (10 means 10%), 0..100
value.returns: total sales tax in integer cents, rounded half up to the cent
value.errors: KeyError if region is a string not present in rates.csv; ValueError if discount_pct is outside 0..100 or an amount is not an int
value.tax_rate_lookup: tax.tax_pct(region) -> float percent number; KeyError if not found

why: Lines carry category so tax.py can apply exemptions; region and discount come from pricing's customer record; money in cents, percents as percent numbers per team standard.

value: region=None (unknown customer) -> tax 0 cents; unknown non-None region string -> KeyError
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0% tax, but the team standard says a failed lookup raises KeyError. This separates the two: an unknown customer is signalled by region=None and gives 0; a region code missing from rates.csv is a data error and raises KeyError.

value.pricing.sku_exists(sku) -> bool: True if sku is in the item table (needed because price 0 is a valid price)
value.pricing.discount_multiplier(cid) -> Deci: 10% off is Decimal("0.90"); unknown customer returns Decimal("1") (= 0% discount; a 0 default would mean 100% off)
value.tax.tax_rate(cid) -> Decimal: multiplier, 8.25% is Decimal("1.0825"); unknown customer returns Decimal("1") (0%)
value.tax.tax_amount(cid, lines, discount_mult: lines = list of (sku, line_amount Decimal) for KNOWN skus only, pre-discount; tax.py decides taxability per sku and how the discount applies to the taxable base; returns tax in dollars, rounded to the cent, ROUND_HALF_UP
value.invoice.render_invoice(order) -> str: invoice.py rounds the discount (subtotal*(1-m) to cent, ROUND_HALF_UP), formats percents without trailing zeros, never computes tax rules

why: Concrete API for the three modules. Keeps the team standard (Decimal dollars, multipliers, default-on-miss) with two explicit exceptions: sku_exists (0 is a valid price) and discount/tax multiplier default 1 (0 would mean 100% off). Tax takes per-line amounts and the discount multiplier because the example tax 1.86 only works if tax applies to the discounted taxable line A (22.50 * 8.25%), not to the whole subtotal.

tax.py needs money as integer cents and percents as percent numbers (team standard). Please change price to int cents (e.g. 1250 = $12.50) and discount to a percent number (10 = 10%). Region None for unknown customers is fine for me. I accept everything else in pricing_api.
Superseded: pricing_api (agent1) and TAX_API (agent2) already cover these functions. Withdrawing so the open proposals can close; I will work from those.

Accept. Unknown customer -> region None -> 0 tax, and invoice shows 0% tax.
